events.title: Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling is shown to the public
events.description: After four years of work, Michelangelo's ceiling frescoes in the Sistine Chapel were unveiled for the feast of All Saints. Its scenes from Genesis, including the Creation of Adam, became a pinnacle of Renaissance art.
events.html: After four years of work, Michelangelo's ceiling frescoes in the Sistine Chapel were unveiled for the feast of All Saints. Its scenes from Genesis, including the Creation of Adam, became a pinnacle of Renaissance art.

events.title: Othello is performed before James I at Whitehall
events.description: The King's Men performed Shakespeare's Othello in the Banqueting House at Whitehall, the earliest recorded performance of the play. Its tragedy of jealousy and manipulation remains among his most performed works.
events.html: The King's Men performed Shakespeare's Othello in the Banqueting House at Whitehall, the earliest recorded performance of the play. Its tragedy of jealousy and manipulation remains among his most performed works.

events.title: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Lisbon
events.description: On All Saints' Day a massive earthquake, followed by a tsunami and fires, destroyed most of Lisbon and killed tens of thousands. The catastrophe stirred Enlightenment debates on providence and spurred early seismology.
events.html: On All Saints' Day a massive earthquake, followed by a tsunami and fires, destroyed most of Lisbon and killed tens of thousands. The catastrophe stirred Enlightenment debates on providence and spurred early seismology.

events.title: John Adams becomes the first president to live in the White House
events.description: John Adams moved into the unfinished President's House in Washington. The next day he wrote to his wife Abigail: 'May none but honest and wise men ever rule under this roof.'
events.html: John Adams moved into the unfinished President's House in Washington. The next day he wrote to his wife Abigail: 'May none but honest and wise men ever rule under this roof.'

events.title: The first medical school for women opens in Boston
events.description: Samuel Gregory opened the Boston Female Medical School, later the New England Female Medical College, with twelve students. It was the first institution founded to train women in medicine.
events.html: Samuel Gregory opened the Boston Female Medical School, later the New England Female Medical College, with twelve students. It was the first institution founded to train women in medicine.

events.title: Von Spee's squadron defeats the Royal Navy at Coronel
events.description: Off the coast of Chile, Admiral Maximilian von Spee's German East Asia Squadron sank two British cruisers, killing Rear-Admiral Cradock and some 1,600 men. It was Britain's first naval defeat in a century.

events.title: The Maastricht Treaty creates the European Union
events.description: The Treaty on European Union came into force, establishing the EU alongside the European Communities. It introduced EU citizenship and set the path to economic and monetary union and the euro.
